evals.name: plain-readme
evals.prompt: Can you turn the README at evals/fixtures/plain-readme.md into a nice PDF I can share with the team? It's the readme for our parqet CLI tool. No diagrams in it, just headings, an options table, and a couple of code blocks.
evals.expected_output: A designed A4 PDF in both light and dark themes rendered from the parqet README: a cover from the title, sectioned prose, the options table styled, and the install/usage code blocks syntax-highlighted. No content runs off the page.
assertions: A light-theme PDF is produced by default (dark is opt-in — produced only when the reader asks for one).
Each PDF is a valid, non-empty PDF that opens and has at least one page.
No content is clipped or runs off the page edge on any page, in either theme.
Output looks intentionally designed (cover/title treatment, clear section hierarchy, consistent styling) rather than a raw markdown dump.
The options/flags table renders as a real styled table with all its rows and columns intact.
The install and usage code blocks render as syntax-highlighted code blocks (monospaced, distinct from body text).
[with_skill only] The authored pdf.tsx imports only from '@docsmith/docsmith' with no relative imports or local asset files.

evals.name: mermaid-spec
evals.prompt: I need to export our webhook delivery design spec to a polished PDF for the architecture review. The doc is at evals/fixtures/mermaid-spec.md and it has two mermaid diagrams (a flowchart and a sequence diagram) that absolutely need to show up as real diagrams, not code blocks.
evals.expected_output: A designed A4 PDF in both themes where both mermaid diagrams render as actual vector diagrams fully inside their cards (nothing clipped), the prose is sectioned, and the retry/backoff content reads cleanly. No overflow in either theme.
assertions: A light-theme PDF is produced by default (dark is opt-in — produced only when the reader asks for one).
Each PDF is a valid, non-empty PDF that opens and has at least one page.
No content is clipped or runs off the page edge on any page, in either theme.
Output looks intentionally designed (cover/title treatment, clear section hierarchy, consistent styling) rather than a raw markdown dump.
The delivery flowchart appears as an actual rendered diagram (nodes and arrows), not as a code/text block and not a blank box.
The sequence diagram appears as an actual rendered diagram (participants and messages), not as code and not blank.
Both diagrams sit fully inside their cards/containers with nothing clipped at the card or page edge.
[with_skill only] The authored pdf.tsx imports only from '@docsmith/docsmith' with no relative imports or local asset files.

evals.name: rich-designed
evals.prompt: Make this payments migration decision brief look really sharp as a PDF — it's going to leadership. It's at evals/fixtures/rich-designed.md. There's a recommendation, a comparison of three options, a side-by-side table, some risks, and a phased rollout plan. Use whatever design elements make it look professional.
evals.expected_output: A designed A4 PDF in both themes that reaches for the richer components where they fit: e.g. the option comparison as compare/panel cards, the recommendation/risk callouts as key boxes, badges for status, the rollout as a phase sequence, and the side-by-side as a styled table. Looks designed, not just formatted markdown. No overflow.
assertions: A light-theme PDF is produced by default (dark is opt-in — produced only when the reader asks for one).
Each PDF is a valid, non-empty PDF that opens and has at least one page.
No content is clipped or runs off the page edge on any page, in either theme.
Output looks intentionally designed (cover/title treatment, clear section hierarchy, consistent styling) rather than a raw markdown dump.
The three options (in-house, Stripe, PayPal) are presented as visually distinct cards or panels, not just plain paragraphs.
The recommendation and/or risks are surfaced as styled callouts/key-boxes, not buried in body text.
The four-step rollout plan is presented as a phase/step sequence treatment, not a plain numbered list.
The side-by-side dimensions table renders as a styled comparison table with all five rows.
[with_skill only] The authored pdf.tsx imports only from '@docsmith/docsmith' with no relative imports or local asset files.

evals.name: long-multipage

evals.expected_output: A multi-page designed A4 PDF in both themes that paginates cleanly: sections flow across pages with no content clipped at page edges and no mostly-empty pages / large gaps. Consistent styling throughout both themes.
assertions: A light-theme PDF is produced by default (dark is opt-in — produced only when the reader asks for one).
Each PDF is a valid, non-empty PDF that opens and has at least one page.
No content is clipped or runs off the page edge on any page, in either theme.
Output looks intentionally designed (cover/title treatment, clear section hierarchy, consistent styling) rather than a raw markdown dump.
The document spans multiple pages (at least 3).
